AAP News.title: Review confirms HPV vaccine is safe, effective

AAP News.title: New approaches can improve access to more devices for children

AAP News.title: Safe storage of marijuana an issue, even in states where it’s still illegal

AAP News.title: How to help families choose decision-making support before youths with disabilities become adults
AAP News.author: Megyn Sebesta, D.O., FAAP, and Sarah Northrop, M.D., FAAP
AAP News.first_paragraph: Medical and legal processes should be considered when pediatricians assist families and youths with intellectual or developmental disabilities in transitioning to adult care.

AAP News.title: Letter to the editor: Have empathic, forthright discussions as youths with disabilities enter transitional care phase
AAP News.author: N/A

AAP News.title: Led by pediatricians, Grandparents for Vaccines advocates for childhood vaccination

AAP News.title: More than 3,000 medical students match to pediatric residencies, AAP leaders call for workforce growth
AAP News.author: Steve Schering, Staff Writer, and Sean Stangland, Associate Editor
AAP News.first_paragraph: Thousands of medical students discovered their residency destinations during Match Day 2026, including more than 3,000 pediatric students who will be entering the workforce pipeline.

AAP News.title: Pediatricians eye congressional seats to advocate for children’s health
AAP News.author: Steve Schering, Staff Writer
AAP News.first_paragraph: Pediatricians Richard J. Pan, M.D., M.P.H., FAAP, of California, and Annie L. Andrews, M.D., M.S., of South Carolina, are waging primary battles for seats in Congress.

AAP News.title: Perioral dermatitis in children: A childhood form of rosacea
AAP News.author: Sarah Asch, M.D., FAAD, FAAP, and Sarah L. Stein, M.D., FAAD, FAAP
AAP News.first_paragraph: Better understanding of the mechanisms of perioral dermatitis has led to a broader array of treatment options for children.

AAP News.title: Help families set achievable goals to increase children’s physical activity
AAP News.author: Sarah Hoffman, D.O., FAAP
AAP News.first_paragraph: Both well and sick visits with a primary care pediatrician as well as subspecialty visits can be excellent opportunities for exercise counseling.

AAP News.title: Silver diamine fluoride is a powerful tool to stop dental caries
AAP News.author: Erica Caffrey, D.D.S., and Steve Holve, M.D., FAAP
AAP News.first_paragraph: Application of silver diamine fluoride can be learned easily through training videos and observation.

AAP News.title: Belief and faith will lift us up and carry us forward
AAP News.first_paragraph: AAP President Andrew D. Racine, M.D., Ph.D., FAAP, calls for embracing belief in science and faith in each other, our practices and our communities.

AAP News.title: Academy advocates for environmental health amid regulatory rollbacks
AAP News.first_paragraph: Environmental health continues to be a critical advocacy priority for the AAP, especially as the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has taken major steps to unravel key measures designed to minimize the impacts of climate change and ensure children can breathe clean air.

AAP News.title: Children with sleep apnea are twice as likely to be infected with flu, COVID-19
AAP News.first_paragraph: Researchers examined five years’ worth of EHR data for more than a million children ages 2-18.

AAP News.first_paragraph: A longitudinal study followed 460,000 teens in a California health system.

AAP News.title: Registration opens for the 2026 AAP National Conference & Exhibition in San Diego
AAP News.first_paragraph: AAP members get the best rates for the event returning to California with more than 350 educational sessions.

AAP News.title: Dr. Vinci focuses on future of pediatric workforce as he accepts St. Geme award
AAP News.first_paragraph: Robert J. Vinci, M.D., FAAP, was recognized for contributions to reshape pediatric education, pediatric workforce policy and access to care for vulnerable populations.

AAP News.title: South Carolina’s measles outbreak ends after nearly 1,000 cases, 21 hospitalizations
AAP News.first_paragraph: Local officials credit a recent increase in vaccinations for helping to end the outbreak. Doses increased 94% in Spartanburg County and 82% in the Upstate region compared to the same time period a year earlier.

AAP News.title: AAP survey: Anxiety, depression a core part of care, but pediatricians face barriers
AAP News.first_paragraph: Most reported caring for children with anxiety and depression at least weekly and agreed that lack of time and resources are barriers.

AAP News.title: Report offers ways to integrate mental health as part of overall care
AAP News.first_paragraph: A new clinical report provides a framework for integrating mental health care into practice by leveraging existing skills and relationships, identifying concerns early and supporting children and families across the full spectrum of development.

AAP News.title: CDC: 44 more measles cases reported; four states report first 2026 cases
AAP News.first_paragraph: The CDC also reports six more pediatric flu deaths among children, though flu activity in most parts of the U.S. is minimal.

AAP News.title: CDC: ED visits for tick bites highest in a decade
AAP News.first_paragraph: Children under 10 years have the highest rates of ED visits for tick bites this year.

AAP News.title: 5,000 youth ATVs recalled following death of 6-year-old rider
AAP News.first_paragraph: Nearly 5,000 youth ATVs are being recalled because of mechanical and safety failures after the death of a 6-year-old rider last year.

AAP News.title: AAP policy statement includes list of essential emergency equipment for primary care offices
AAP News.first_paragraph: AAP policy urges primary care pediatricians to create emergency protocols, stock essential equipment and practice scenarios with staff.

AAP News.title: Measles cases reach 76% of last year’s total; pediatric flu deaths rise to 143
AAP News.first_paragraph: South Carolina’s measles outbreak has slowed, national flu activity is low and RSV is elevated but appears to have peaked, according to CDC data.

AAP News.title: AAP urges federal officials to remove immigration barriers for international medical graduates
AAP News.first_paragraph: Administrative delays are keeping medical students, resident physicians and practicing physicians from entering the U.S. or remaining in the country during a time when there is a physician shortage.

AAP News.title: AAP program helps early career pediatricians connect, lead
AAP News.first_paragraph: The AAP’s Early Career Leadership Institute brings participants together for webinars, coaching sessions and other projects. It has been streamlined and adapted to best meet the needs of future physician leaders.

AAP News.title: More than 100 medical groups say changes to ACIP ‘potentially jeopardizing access to life-saving vaccines’
AAP News.first_paragraph: The new charter for the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices puts more focus on rare vaccine injuries, broadens the qualifications for members and adds liaison organizations known for spreading false information about vaccines.

AAP News.title: Measles cases top 1,700 as CDC reports 12 additional pediatric flu deaths
AAP News.first_paragraph: Reported measles cases have risen to 1,714 as the United States approaches the record 2,287 cases reported all of last year, according to the CDC.

AAP News.title: ABP revises essential tasks for pediatricians
AAP News.first_paragraph: The updated essential tasks are part of a framework to support pediatric programs in preparing new graduates for independent practice.

AAP News.title: AAP requests urgent access to immigrant detention center amid growing reports of dangers to children
AAP News.first_paragraph: The AAP wants to ensure immigrant children at the family detention center in Dilley, Texas, are receiving crucial medical care.

AAP News.title: USDA retracts warning for lead in dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets
AAP News.first_paragraph: Frozen, dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets sold at Walmart do not contain elevated levels of lead or pose a health concern, federal officials said.

AAP News.title: Measles cases already reach 75% of last year’s record-breaking total, CDC reports
AAP News.first_paragraph: The RSV immunization period has been extended by most states as the CDC reports 96 additional measles cases and four new pediatric influenza-associated deaths.

AAP News.title: FDA: Supplements marketed as stimulants contain harmful, life-threatening ingredients
AAP News.published_date:
Publisher: American Academy of Pediatrics
 April 03, 2026

AAP News.title: Most states extending RSV immunization season for eligible infants and toddlers
AAP News.first_paragraph: RSV season got a late start, and activity has been elevated later than usual. Most states are allowing immunization to continue through April.

AAP News.title: Study: Cleaning product injuries sent 240,000 young children to EDs from 2007-’22
AAP News.first_paragraph: Detergent packets and spray bottles were the main culprits. Authors called for safer packaging, public education and reducing children's access to these products.

AAP News.title: USDA: Frozen dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets may be contaminated with lead
AAP News.first_paragraph: The nuggets were sold at Walmart stores nationwide. They are no longer on the shelves but may still be in people’s freezers.

AAP News.title: FYI: Revamped PREP material, virtual course on pediatric mental health, new nutrition content
AAP News.first_paragraph: PREP Blocks offers a customizable PREP learning experience; a one-day intensive course looks at mental health care issues; updated and expanded patient care page offers AAP resources on nutrition.

AAP News.title: Why we give the hepatitis B vaccine at birth
AAP News.first_paragraph: The AAP continues to recommend the birth dose of hepatitis B for all infants.

AAP News.title: Educating families on risks for scald burns can help prevent injuries in children
AAP News.first_paragraph: Because young children have thinner skin, they develop deeper burns at lower temperatures.

AAP News.title: New AAP chief medical officer’s goal: ‘To provide support to the team, to the organization and to our members’
AAP News.first_paragraph: Lee Savio Beers, M.D., FAAP, outlines priorities in her new role, including ways to build on the Academy’s robust foundation while meeting new challenges and supporting members caring for children and families.

AAP News.title: Educating next generation of pediatricians drives new AAP board member Dr. Peltier
AAP News.first_paragraph: New AAP board member Christopher B. Peltier, M.D., FAAP, hopes to use his role to develop support and guidance for those who educate future pediatricians.

AAP News.title: Child behavior and disrupted caregiving: pediatricians can help build safe, stable, nurturing relationships
AAP News.first_paragraph: Over time, exposure to disrupted caregiving can affect a child’s developing regulatory systems, impacting psychological, behavioral and neurodevelopmental outcomes.

AAP News.title: State-level pediatric councils identify payment issues, aim to improve coverage for care
AAP News.first_paragraph: A state chapter pediatric council brings together pediatricians, pediatric medical subspecialists, and pediatric surgical specialists to build relationships and foster open dialogue with commercial payers and their state’s Medicaid authority.

AAP News.title: AAP study highlights preparedness, gaps in graduating residents’ mental health training
AAP News.first_paragraph: The AAP examined survey data from graduating residents on their preparedness to care for overall mental health needs and a range of specific conditions affecting children and adolescents.

AAP News.title: EHR advancements should prompt review of privacy policies
AAP News.first_paragraph: The complexity and volume of data being collected, including wearables, patient-reported outcomes and questionnaires, and ambient listening tools, pose new challenges to health systems for how they process and share this information.

AAP News.title: Symposium that followed wildfires can be model for chapters to provide climate change education
AAP News.first_paragraph: By creating platforms for learning, sharing and advocacy, chapters can empower their communities to make informed decisions about climate change.

AAP News.title: Do recent changes to federal vaccine recommendations affect clinician liability?
AAP News.first_paragraph: Recent changes to the CDC immunization schedule have raised questions about medicolegal risk, but the fundamental liability landscape for clinicians has not changed.

AAP News.title: Thinking of Lenore: Creating a health care infrastructure worthy of all children
AAP News.first_paragraph: We must invest in our nation’s health care infrastructure to optimize health and well-being for all children.

AAP News.first_paragraph: While promoting immunizations is not new for the Academy, the scale and resources of its campaign to promote evidence-based vaccine recommendations have had broader impacts on legislation, online discourse and in pediatricians’ offices across the country.

AAP News.title: Study: 71% of infant, toddler food products commonly found at grocery stores are ultra-processed
AAP News.first_paragraph: Consumption of ultra-processed food during complementary feeding could shape adult habits, increasing chances of obesity, cardiovascular disease and other conditions.

AAP News.first_paragraph: Parents of Black and Hispanic children are more likely to say they can’t afford swimming lessons and to have poor swimming safety knowledge themselves.

AAP News.title: AAP, health groups sue EPA for allowing more toxic power plant emissions
AAP News.first_paragraph: The groups are suing the EPA for rolling back clean air standards, a move that will be harmful to children’s lungs and brain development.

AAP News.title: Measles cases already 69% of last year’s total; flu rates dip below baseline
AAP News.first_paragraph: RSV rates remain elevated nationally but are declining in most states.

AAP News.title: Outbreak of E. coli linked to raw dairy products
AAP News.first_paragraph: Nine people in three states have been infected with  E. coli  and more than half are children younger than 5.

AAP News.title: Young children see drop in rates for 5 vaccines including flu, HepB birth dose
AAP News.first_paragraph: Rates held steady for other vaccines included in CDC analysis of 2024 data.

AAP News.title: What to do when parents ask for treatment that may not be beneficial for child with life-threatening condition
AAP News.first_paragraph: An AAP clinical report and technical report emphasize collaboration between clinicians and families, and encourage open communication to understand family values, goals and fears.

AAP News.first_paragraph: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) rates also are elevated but decreasing in much of the country.

AAP News.title: Nearly 90,000 bottles of children’s ibuprofen recalled
AAP News.first_paragraph: The recall follows complaints of a “gel-like mass and black particles in the product.”

AAP News.title: AAP's historic victory in vaccine lawsuit a 'critical step' in restoring science to federal policy
AAP News.first_paragraph: A federal judge granted the AAP’s request to block implementation of the new federal immunization schedule for children and decisions made by new federal vaccine advisers while the case continues.

AAP News.title: GRADE framework helps evaluate quality of evidence to develop recommendations
AAP News.first_paragraph: The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) tool is used or endorsed by 120 organizations worldwide to help authors evaluate the quality of evidence while accounting for contextual factors.

AAP News.title: New clinical practice guideline defines ‘faltering weight,’ recommends treatment options
AAP News.first_paragraph: The clinical practice guideline uses the new term “faltering weight” instead of “failure to thrive,” which has no precise definition, is stigmatizing and has unclear standards of care.

AAP News.title: New faltering weight guidance impacts coding, reporting, documentation
AAP News.first_paragraph: Accurately selecting and reporting codes for patients with faltering weight ensures the full scope of the clinician’s work is captured, supports proper payment and helps maintain precise documentation of the child’s medical needs and treatments.

AAP News.title: 81 more measles cases, 11 more pediatric flu deaths confirmed by CDC

AAP News.title: Pediatricians face challenges as vaccine-preventable diseases spread

AAP News.title: AAP: CDC vaccine advisers missing opportunities to talk about measles, flu, RSV
AAP News.first_paragraph: AAP’s president outlined “deep concerns” about the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices meeting planned for March 18-19.

AAP News.title: How to make immunizations part of pediatric surgical, procedural care process
AAP News.first_paragraph: Providing immunizations during the perioperative or periprocedural period helps more children get vaccines when they need them.

AAP News.title: Survey finds people trust their doctor, AAP more than federal health agencies
AAP News.first_paragraph: About 86% of respondents expressed confidence in their primary care provider, 77% in the AAP and 60% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

AAP News.title: RSV rates rising instead of winding down in some states
AAP News.first_paragraph: Nationwide, 9.1% of tests were positive as of Feb. 28, the highest so far this season. Experts are encouraging continued immunizations for young children.

AAP News.title: Measles cases rise to 1,281; pediatric flu deaths rise to 90
AAP News.first_paragraph: Surging measles cases and a highly severe flu season underscore the need to boost vaccination rates.

AAP News.title: FDA approves first generic version of Flovent asthma inhaler
AAP News.first_paragraph: The fluticasone propionate product is an inhaled corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lungs and can be used as a maintenance treatment of asthma in patients 4 years and older.

AAP News.title: AAP files lawsuit over Florida AG’s attempt to suppress ‘essential medical discourse’
AAP News.first_paragraph: AAP leaders say the Florida attorney general's legal attack on its gender-affirming care guidance violates the First Amendment.

AAP News.title: Autism research leaders form independent group amid concern over government committee
AAP News.first_paragraph: The new Independent Autism Coordinating Committee said its goal is “accelerating scientific discovery, improving care, and positively impacting the lives of people with autism.”

AAP News.title: Report: Declining measles vaccination could cost $7.8 billion by 2030
AAP News.first_paragraph: Declining measles vaccination rates could lead to 17,000 infections, 4,000 hospitalizations and 36 preventable deaths each year from 2026-2030.

AAP News.first_paragraph: Federal officials have announced the recall of products that may be harmful.

AAP News.title: 5-step approach to conflictual conversations can improve care, reduce liability risk
AAP News.first_paragraph: Escalating conflicts with families can cause emotional distress for clinicians and care teams, heighten the risk of errors or omissions, and lead to malpractice claims.

AAP News.title: In memoriam: Susan S. Aronson, former AAP board member, Pennsylvania Chapter president
AAP News.first_paragraph: Former AAP board member Susan S. Aronson, M.D., FAAP, of Stuart, Fla, died Dec. 22, 2025, at age 84.

AAP News.title: In memoriam: Edward N. Bailey, former AAP board member, Massachusetts chapter president
AAP News.first_paragraph: Former AAP board member Edward N. Bailey, M.D., FAAP, of Springfield, Mass., died Jan. 28 at age 81.

AAP News.title: In memoriam: William Foege, former CDC director, honorary AAP fellow
AAP News.first_paragraph: Former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), William H. Foege, M.D., M.P.H., FAAP (Hon.), of Atlanta, died Jan. 24 at age 89.

AAP News.title: Advocacy Spotlight: AAP helps shape new federal safety standards for water beads, neck floats, bassinets
AAP News.first_paragraph: New rules will force manufacturers to create products with lower risk of injury or death.

AAP News.title: Dr. Vinci to receive 2026 St. Geme Leadership Award
AAP News.first_paragraph: The award recognizes the leadership of Robert J. Vinci, M.D., FAAP, as a clinician, educator, mentor and institutional builder whose contributions have reshaped pediatric education, pediatric workforce policy and access to care for vulnerable populations.

AAP News.title: AAP dedicates resources to set the record straight on vaccines
AAP News.first_paragraph: The AAP’s campaign to promote confidence in vaccines has engaged people on social media, provided resources for physicians and elevated voices promoting evidence-based recommendations.

AAP News.title: AAP survey: 99% of pediatric residents have positions when they graduate
AAP News.first_paragraph: Only 3% of graduating residents reported considerable difficulty in their search for a position, while 54% reported no difficulty.

AAP News.title: Correct coding needed for behind-the-scenes work to care for children with complex medical needs
AAP News.first_paragraph: Accurate coding can help easy payment for significant behind-the-scenes work in caring for children with complex medical needs.

AAP News.title: Animating principle of our advocacy: All children are like our own
AAP News.first_paragraph: Our patients are in many ways “our own” children. Families know this, which is one reason they place such profound trust in our advice about how to care for their children.

AAP News.title: Federal government’s 2026 funding bill delivers on AAP priorities
AAP News.first_paragraph: Key programs and bills expand access to pediatric health care, firearm injury prevention research, Medicaid funding for children with complex health care needs and more.

AAP News.title: Virtual sick visits more likely to need ED follow-up than in-person visits

AAP News.title: Study: Law banning e-cigarette flavors had little effect on teens’ habits

AAP News.title: How to help patients with developmental disabilities when they age out of pediatric systems
AAP News.first_paragraph: Transition considerations include higher education and employment training, accessing therapy outside of public education systems, transferring care to adult providers, decision-making support and community integration.

AAP News.title: Transient, orthostatic, persistent: How to distinguish among types of proteinuria
AAP News.first_paragraph: Most proteinuria in children is transient or orthostatic and does not require nephrology referral, but early detection of persistent proteinuria is critical.

AAP News.title: Few AI-enabled medical devices for children authorized by FDA
AAP News.first_paragraph: Only about 4% of devices include patients younger than 18 years in their indications for use statements.

AAP News.title: Just 1.3% of teens’ ED encounters included HIV testing
AAP News.first_paragraph: Researchers examined data from more than 2 million ED visits over a five-year period.

AAP News.title: What happens when students don’t land their ideal residency?

AAP News.title: Responding to questions about immigration enforcement requires empathy, honesty

AAP News.title: More than 200 organizations announce support for AAP vaccine schedule

AAP News.title: Study: At least 50 infants died in inclined sleepers after recall
AAP News.first_paragraph: Authors encouraged more education about recalls and safe sleep for parents and caregivers.

AAP News.first_paragraph: The technical report documents how Medicaid has improved access to care, reduced unnecessary utilization and improved long-term health and educational outcomes for children with coverage, as well as how it has reduced health inequities.

AAP News.title: New safety data inform updated AAP policy on pediatric anesthesia
AAP News.first_paragraph: The updated policy reaffirms that facility readiness, team training, continuous practice improvement and individual efforts toward pediatric-specific continuing education are important for safe periprocedural care.

AAP News.title: Updated policy on adolescent confidentiality addresses new technology, range of sensitive data
AAP News.first_paragraph: Adolescent confidentiality is one of the most complex aspects of pediatric care. This complexity is driven by both state and federal laws.

AAP News.title: Confirmed measles cases approach 1,000 for the year; 5 more pediatric flu deaths reported
AAP News.published_date:
Publisher: American Academy of Pediatrics

Arab News.title: Man convicted in terrorism trial over the 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie
Arab News.first_paragraph:
A man was convicted Wednesday of federal terrorism charges in the 2022 stabbing of Salman Rushdie, the author who has faced a decades-old death threat over his novel “The Satanic Verses.”

After just a couple of hours of deliberations, a jury found Hadi Matar guilty of all the charges against him, including engaging in an act of transnational terrorism.

Rushdie, who was about to speak on writers’ safety, was slashed 15 times on an amphitheater stage in 2022. He was gravely wounded and lost the sight in his right eye.

Prosecutors asserted that Matar was motivated by the late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini ‘s 1989 call for Rushdie’s death because of “The Satanic Verses.”

“His brutal attack on Mr. Rushdie during a peaceful speaking event is a chilling reminder of the global reach of Iranian terrorism,” Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg said in a statement after the verdict, adding that “justice has been done.” Iran’s government has denied involvement in the attack.

Matar’s defense: No evidence of his state of mind

Messages seeking comment on the verdict were sent to Matar’s attorneys and Rushdie’s assistant. During the trial, defense lawyer Nathaniel Barone said the government had no proof of what was in Matar’s head.

Matar himself declined to testify. Rushdie did, telling jurors: “I can’t say what his ambitions or his aim was, but the wounds were dispersed across my body.”

Matar, 28, is already serving a 25-year New York state prison sentence on an attempted murder conviction in the stabbing. His federal sentencing is set for Nov. 3, when he faces a potential life term.

Rushdie won Britain’s prestigious Booker Prize for his 1981 novel “Midnight’s Children,” about his native India. “The Satanic Verses,” a novel of magical realism about the lives and dreams of two actors who survive a plane explosion, followed in 1988.

It drew critical acclaim in the United Kingdom but engendered protests around the Muslim world over what some believers saw as blasphemous suggestions about Islam’s Prophet Muhammad, particularly in a dream sequence. Over the ensuing years, at least 45 people were killed in riots over the book, a Japanese translator was stabbed to death, and an Italian translator and Norwegian publisher were attacked.

Rushdie, who was born into a Muslim family, has said the dream sequence was just that. But he went into hiding for years, gradually emerging after Iran’s government distanced itself in 1998 from Khomeini’s fatwa, or religious edict.

“For two decades or more, I led a public life without a hint of trouble,” Rushdie testified at the trial in Buffalo, New York.

Yet the fatwa was never rescinded; indeed, Khomenei’s successor, the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, indicated in 2017 that it remained in effect. An Iranian foundation has offered a more than $3 million bounty for killing Rushdie.

Prosecutors: Matar’s messages showed him zeroing in on Rushdie

Matar broached the fatwa with contacts in messaging apps in 2021 and 2022, according to exhibits shown in court. The messages showed Matar fuming that he felt Rushdie had attacked Islam and, by surviving, emboldened others to insult the faith. Matar alluded to a 2006 comment along those lines by the late Hezbollah militant group leader Hassan Nasrallah, the messages showed.

Born in the US, Matar also holds citizenship in Lebanon, where Hezbollah is based. Prosecutors said that photos in Matar’s New Jersey bedroom and on his computer indicated his support for Hezbollah, which the US has designated a terrorist organization.

Matar “spent months planning and preparing to carry out what he hoped would be the execution of Salman Rushdie,” US Attorney Michael DiGiacomo said in a statement Wednesday.

The messages showed Matar initially talked about wanting to “expose” Rushdie, then about taking his life. In a private note to himself, he wrote: “We need to kill him ASAP,” Assistant US Attorney Timothy Lynch said in an opening statement on July 22. The prosecutor said Matar framed the planned killing as part of what he considered a jihad, or holy war.

By spring 2022, the electronic chats showed, Matar wrote that he had discerned where Rushdie lived and was tracking his public appearances, eventually pointing out his scheduled August 2022 talk at the Chautauqua Institution, a western New York arts and intellectual center.

As Rushdie was being introduced, his attacker climbed on stage behind him, then stabbed him as the audience gasped. Spectators and another speaker, Henry Reese, scrambled to aid Rushdie. Law enforcement officers, assigned to the event, arrested the attacker — soon identified as Matar — after civilians restrained him.

Rushdie published a 2024 memoir about the attack, then returned to fiction with last year’s “The Eleventh Hour.” The author, who was knighted by Britain’s late Queen Elizabeth II, received a Dayton Literary Peace Prize lifetime achievement award in November.

Arab News.title: US awards $58.6 billion Patriot missile contract amid rising stockpile concerns
Arab News.first_paragraph:
WASHINGTON: The US Defense Department awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6 billion to produce Patriot interceptor missiles, the Pentagon said on Wednesday, as ​conflicts in Iran and Ukraine strain US weapons stockpiles.

The US has supplied large quantities of weapons to allies while also using munitions in its own military operations in Iran, raising concerns about inventories of key air defense and precision-guided weapons.

The Lockheed award converts a previous one-year deal worth $4.7 billion awarded in April into a seven-year draft agreement, creating a multiyear procurement plan for the interceptors from fiscal 2026 ‌through 2032, the ‌military said.

Pentagon negotiators are pressing contractors ​to ‌move ⁠much faster, with ​tentative ⁠production agreements struck earlier this year at the center of efforts to increase missile output. The administration of President Donald Trump has also steadily increased pressure on defense contractors to prioritize production over shareholder payouts. Trump signed an executive order in January to identify contractors deemed to be underperforming on government contracts while continuing to distribute profits to shareholders.

Industry executives have welcomed ⁠the production agreements, but said Congress must first appropriate ‌funding before companies can invest more heavily ‌in components and production capacity.

Exact terms and delivery ​dates for many Pentagon munitions deals ‌are still under negotiation.

A similar framework deal had been struck ‌with Raytheon’s parent company RTX to boost production of Tomahawk cruise missiles from the current rate of about 60 per year for the US to eventually 1,000 units annually.

Lockheed, a Bethesda, Maryland-based defense contractor, said the funding would allow it ‌to follow through on a promise to triple PAC-3 MSE production capacity by the end of 2030 ⁠and increase jobs ⁠at its Camden, Arkansas, plant by 50 percent, to about 1,850 from 1,200. Lockheed previously announced Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptor production would go to 2,000 units annually.

Lockheed Martin said it is investing $8 billion to $9 billion through 2030 to modernize more than 20 US facilities, including new munitions centers in Alabama and Arkansas.

PAC-3 MSE is a hit-to-kill interceptor used within the Patriot air defense system to counter ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and aircraft.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies, a Washington-based think tank, estimated this week that the US military has fewer than 1,000 ​Patriot interceptors on hand and fewer ​than 250 THAAD interceptors — two key air defense systems. Both have seen recent heavy use in the Middle East.

“With profound sorrow we received the news of the helicopter accident that occurred in our province, in which seven people sadly lost their lives,” San Juan Governor Marcelo Orrego wrote on X.

Arab News.title: Cyprus’ ethnic split must be resolved to stabilize a tumultuous region, UN chief says
Arab News.first_paragraph:
NICOSIA, Cyprus: Resolving Cyprus’ ethnic division is “absolutely crucial” for stabilizing a turbulent region where persistent conflicts have the potential to escalate, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said Wednesday.

Guterres made a rare, two-day visit to Cyprus to underline his commitment to restarting deadlocked peace talks on a deal to end the 52-year-old rift in which a UN- controlled buffer zone separates breakaway Turkish Cypriots in the island’s northern third and Greek Cypriots in the south.

“I do believe that a solution in Cyprus is absolutely crucial, not only to preserve the interests and the peace of the Cyprus people, but also as a factor of stability in what is becoming a dangerously unstable region,” Guterres told a news conference after meeting with the island’s rival leaders.

Cyprus was split in 1974 when Turkiye invaded in the wake of an Athens junta-backed coup whose supporters sought union with Greece. Turkish Cypriots declared independence nearly a decade later, but only Turkiye recognizes it and keeps more than 35,000 troops in the north. Although Cyprus joined the European Union in 2004, only the south where the internationally recognized government is seated enjoys full benefits.

Arab News.title: Spain allows return of fire evacuees to two more towns near Madrid
Arab News.first_paragraph:
MADRID: Residents of the last two towns near Madrid to be fully evacuated because of a massive wildfire were allowed to return home late Wednesday, the interior ministry said in a statement.

The evacuation order imposed on Valdemaqueda and Robledo de Chavela had been lifted “immediately,” it said.

Francisco Martin, the Spanish government’s representative in the Madrid region, said the lifting of the evacuation orders in the two towns “will mean that around 8,500 people will be able to return to their homes.”

Just under 1,000 people remain evacuated from residential areas in two other towns near Madrid, San Martin de Valdeiglesias and Pelayos, he added.

In these two towns only some residential developments were evacuated but the municipality as a whole was not.

Emergency services have been working since last week to put out the blaze in the Madrid region and another in neighboring Avila province, which officials said was the worst in Spain’s recent history.

Earlier Wednesday, the authorities allowed residents to return home to all the towns evacuated due to a wildfire in the province of Avila, west of Madrid.

“I think we are at a point where, with all due caution, we can say that the wildfire is evolving favorably,” Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said late on Wednesday.

But he cautioned the situation remained “critical and highly complex” due to high temperatures, low humidity and strong winds “which are causing fires to spread and expand at an exponential rate.”

“Far faster than what was traditionally considered typical for this type of wildfire,” he added.
