UN News.first_paragraph: Syria is not alone in tackling challenges, including the hundreds of thousands who remain missing during past tumultuous decades, the head of a UN institution said on Thursday as António Guterres departs on his first visit to the country in his current capacity as Secretary-General.

UN News.title: Iran urged to stop protest-related executions
UN News.first_paragraph: Independent UN human rights investigators on Thursday called for Iran to immediately halt the execution of 10 men who took part in a protest in the central city of Isfahan earlier this year, warning that some of their relatives have already been called for final visits.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: New ECOSOC chief, Secretary-General candidates’ debate, torture in Mali, drowning prevention
UN News.first_paragraph: Amar Bendjama, Permanent Representative of Algeria to the UN, was elected on Thursday to serve as the next president of the UN’s Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

UN News.title: Gaza’s food gains could unravel without sustained aid, UN warns
UN News.first_paragraph: Food security and child nutrition have improved across the Gaza Strip largely due to a scale-up in humanitarian assistance and commercial traffic, but progress remains fragile and could quickly reverse without sustained access, funding and recovery support.

UN News.title: Satellites can now spot methane leaks in real time – but most go unfixed
UN News.first_paragraph: Satellites can now spot major methane leaks from space within days. Yet only 13 per cent of those alerts lead to any response from the governments or companies responsible.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: How to turn preventive diplomacy rhetoric into action
UN News.first_paragraph: In the Security Council debate on Thursday on how best to settle disputes between States peacefully, ambassadors provided examples of success and challenges ahead under such themes as effective early warning and how to move from rhetorical support for preventive diplomacy to ensuring more consistent use of its Chapter VI powers under the UN Charter.

UN News.title: Stranded seafarers remain trapped as Hormuz shipping stalls
UN News.first_paragraph: As the Iran-US war continues, the key question remains unanswered about how shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will be managed in future – although the UN has reiterated that charging tolls for safe passage runs contrary to international law.

UN News.title: Thousands prevented from returning home to southern Lebanon
UN News.first_paragraph: As months of conflict continue to devastate communities across Lebanon, families are being left without shelter, healthcare and other essential services.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: Aid for Ukraine, drone attacks in Sudan, DR Congo deaths, neurological disorders in the Americas
UN News.first_paragraph: UN partners launched the Winter Response Plan to help 2.1 million people in Ukraine survive another cold season as the country grapples with the on-going Russian invasion.

UN News.title: Nicaragua continues to weaken political freedoms, UN warns
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Wednesday condemned new threats from Nicaragua’s co-president Daniel Ortega to hinder civil rights and prevent dissenting individuals and groups from participating in elections.

UN News.title: Deadly Afghanistan floods kill at least 26 as aid agencies race to reach survivors
UN News.first_paragraph: Flash floods have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in the mountainous province of Nuristan, where homes, markets and roads were swept away and search teams continued looking for people reported missing.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: Can critical minerals fuel peace and prosperity instead of conflict?
UN News.first_paragraph: The Security Council met Wednesday in New York to debate critical minerals — the lithium, cobalt and copper powering the clean energy transition. Demand is set to triple by 2030. The question: will this mineral wealth build peace and prosperity, or fund conflict and corruption? Follow live updates throughout the day below and go here for full coverage from across the UN.

UN News.title: From lithium to nickel: How the UN is helping countries make the most of critical minerals
UN News.first_paragraph: The world's shift to clean energy is driving huge demand for critical minerals such as lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.

UN News.title: Critical minerals: The hidden resources powering the clean energy future
UN News.first_paragraph: Why are critical minerals suddenly at the centre of global politics?

UN News.title: ‘Business as usual is a business of death’: UN adopts road safety pledge over US objection
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN General Assembly closed its first ever High-level Meeting on road safety on Tuesday by adopting a sweeping new declaration aimed at halving road deaths by 2030 – over the sole objection of the United States.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: Sexual violence in DR Congo, deaths in Ukraine and Russia, crime in Southeast Asia
UN News.first_paragraph: Independent UN human rights experts on Tuesday condemned the M23 armed group’s “reign of terror” over territory it controls in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), calling for an end to the Rwanda-backed group’s sexual torture and violence against civilians.

UN News.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza intensify amid surge of West Bank settler violence
UN News.first_paragraph: Amid intensified deadly Israeli attacks in Gaza, the UN chief and top officials condemned the killings while a surge violence rocked the West Bank and aid agencies scrambled to help Palestinians.

UN News.title: Guterres calls for stepping up diplomatic efforts to end US-Iran conflict
UN News.first_paragraph: The United Nations again called for restraint as war ramps up in the Middle East, underscoring the need for dialogue and an end to attacks on “vital infrastructure” across the region.

UN News.title: Global hunger declines again but progress remains uneven across regions
UN News.first_paragraph: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025 showing that progress is possible, but gains remain fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by the 2030 deadline.

UN News.title: UN refugee agency reports 144 migrants dead or missing off Mauritanian coast
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) reports that 144 migrants attempting to reach Europe are dead or missing due to a series of “tragic maritime incidents” off the coast of Mauritania last week.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: Spotlight on Syria as Guterres heads to Damascus
UN News.first_paragraph: The Security Council discussed the situation on the ground in Syria amid reports of an Israeli attack in occupied territory and of a multi-national oil pipeline to counter the closure of the critical Strait of Hormuz – still the focus of the ongoing US-Iran war. The meeting follows UN independent investigators’ findings that security conditions remain fragile in the south as António Guterres heads to Damascus for his first visit to the country as Secretary-General.

UN News.title: DR Congo: Ebola outbreak still expanding, WHO sees signs of stabilisation
UN News.first_paragraph: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), UN health teams and partners are still racing to contain the rapidly expanding Ebola outbreak despite ongoing insecurity in eastern areas where the virus has taken hold. As of 19 July, the DRC Government has recorded 2,423 confirmed cases, including 967 deaths and 469 recoveries.

UN News.title: From the General Assembly to Harlem: Mandela’s call to action endures
UN News.first_paragraph: Sixty-seven minutes. That is how long volunteers spent serving lunch to people experiencing food insecurity at Refettorio Harlem in New York City last week – one for every year Nelson Mandela gave to public service.

UN News.title: Health response brings lifesaving care closer to thousands in Yemen
UN News.first_paragraph: Thousands of people in some of Yemen's most conflict-affected communities are receiving lifesaving health care closer to home, thanks to funding from the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) through the Yemen Humanitarian Fund.

UN News.title: Ukraine: Deadly Russian attacks severely damage aid warehouses
UN News.first_paragraph: Russian attacks and drone strikes killed at least two children and injured dozens more across Ukraine over recent days while severely damaging three critical aid warehouses, UN agencies reported on Monday.

UN News.title: Middle East: Civilians again under fire as US-Iran strikes continue
UN News.first_paragraph: As the United States and Iran trade deadly attacks for a second week, the UN continues to call for de-escalation while highlighting the devastation caused to civilians and critical infrastructure across the Middle East.

UN News.title: ‘I consider it a miracle’: Pregnant woman pulled from post-quake rubble in Venezuela
UN News.first_paragraph: When a 12-story apartment building pancaked in La Guaira, Venezuela, following two powerful earthquakes late last month, panic ensued to save people injured or trapped under the rubble.

UN News.title: LIVE: Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future
UN News.first_paragraph: Haiti’s future success depends on “security, political engagement, and humanitarian action reinforcing each other,” the UN’s most senior official in Haiti has told the UN Security Council which met in New York on Monday to discuss the way forward for the embattled Caribbean island nation.

UN News.title: Moon Day focuses growing concerns around space junk
UN News.first_paragraph: Amid surging lunar exploration, the UN on Monday urged governments to ensure that humanity's return to the Moon does not come at the expense of planet Earth – or the long-term sustainability of space.

UN News.title: Ukraine: UN condemns overnight attack on Kyiv
UN News.first_paragraph: United Nations agencies have deplored a fresh Russian assault on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv which left at least one person dead and a dozen injured.

UN News.title: Haiti: Signs of hope despite gang violence and political uncertainty
UN News.first_paragraph: For millions of Haitians, daily life has become a struggle to stay safe, find enough food and simply move around their own neighbourhood.

UN News.title: A former Ferrari boss has a blunt message: Your commute is more dangerous than his old job
UN News.first_paragraph: Jean Todt spent decades around the deadliest motorsport on Earth. He was a rally co‑driver, then ran Ferrari’s Formula One team, then became president of world motorsport’s governing body. In his early years, a driver dying at the track barely made news.

UN News.title: Baristas behind bars: Thai prisoners brew a path back to daily life
UN News.first_paragraph: It looks like a regular coffee shop, albeit set up in an old red bus. Stairs lead up to a serving hatch, with a menu of drink options. A selection of jaunty coffee-related messages like “My one and only love: Americano” and “Miss you a latte,” adorn the side of the bus.

UN News.title: US-Iran war: UN chief calls for new diplomatic push following attacks on civilian areas
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN Secretary-General remains deeply concerned by the continuing deadly military escalation between Iran and the United States, his spokesperson said on Friday as attacks destroyed key civilian and military infrastructure across the Gulf region.

UN News.title: Djibouti: Emergency alert spotlights sharp hunger spike
UN News.first_paragraph: More than 256,000 people in Djibouti – around 25 per cent of the population – are likely to face crisis or emergency level hunger over the coming months, a UN-backed global food monitoring network warned in a new report released Friday.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: Appeal for calm in Kashmir, women on the move, Ebola deaths mount, 12th anniversary of MH17
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, has appealed for calm in Pakistan-Administered Kashmir amid unrest ahead of regional elections.

UN News.title: Hunger deepens for displaced families in Sudan’s El Obeid
UN News.first_paragraph: UN humanitarians working in war-torn Sudan on Friday highlighted rapidly growing needs among the more than 100,000 displaced people now sheltering in camps in the city of El Obeid.

UN News.title: Guterres: AI must be shaped by 'all of humanity', not a handful of powers
UN News.first_paragraph: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Friday urged governments and technology companies to work together to ensure artificial intelligence (AI) benefits all countries.

UN News.title: Haiti: Training the next generation to fight corruption
UN News.first_paragraph: How do you tackle corruption in a country grappling with insecurity, weak institutions and widespread impunity? In Haiti, the Government and the United Nations are betting on the country's youth.

UN News.title: Breaking the silence: Zimbabwean youth leader calls for urgent investment in mental health
UN News.first_paragraph: For Tanatswa Amanda Chikaura, mental health advocacy began with a personal loss: while studying psychology at the University of Zimbabwe, she learned that a fellow student had died by suicide.

UN News.title: Venezuela: IOM warns of potential El Niño threat to families displaced by earthquake
UN News.first_paragraph: Thousands of people remain displaced three weeks after the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and the possible formation of a strong El Niño climate pattern could worsen their already dire situation, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) warned on Thursday.

UN News.title: Peacekeepers step up support as families return to south Lebanon
UN News.first_paragraph: With violence in south Lebanon significantly decreased since mid-June, UN peacekeepers there have returned to core functions such as protecting humanitarian aid and restoring critical infrastructure as families continue to return home.

UN News.title: Gaza farmers battle to rebuild as WFP warns of West Bank settler violence
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN is supporting farmers in Gaza who are struggling to rebuild their smallholdings in areas devastated by the Hamas-Israel war.

UN News.title: WHO warns DR Congo Ebola outbreak is outpacing response as Uganda reaches milestone
UN News.first_paragraph: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the third largest on record and is spreading faster than any previous one during the first month of exposure, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday.

UN News.title: As aid dries up, countries pledge to close the $4 trillion development gap
UN News.first_paragraph: UN Member States reaffirmed their commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by adopting a declaration on Wednesday that they will implement reforms to help close the $4 trillion SDG financing gap.

UN News.title: ‘Heat deaths are not inevitable’: WHO pushes Europe to heat‑proof its hospitals
UN News.first_paragraph: As Europe battles a deadly record-breaking heatwave, the World Health Organization (WHO) issued new guidance on Thursday to help countries face scorching temperatures now and in the future.

UN News.title: More than 500 people feared dead in double Myanmar shipwreck tragedy
UN News.first_paragraph: There is growing concern for at least 500 people believed to have been aboard two boats that reportedly capsized off Myanmar’s coast in recent days.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: Schools closed in West Bank, AI in healthcare, Indigenous rights
UN News.first_paragraph: Access to education continues to worsen in the West Bank, the United Nations reported on Wednesday.

UN News.title: Gulf crisis: Guterres calls for de-escalation, warns against return to full-on war
UN News.first_paragraph: UN Secretary-General António Guterres voiced deep concern on Wednesday over the continuing military escalation in the Middle East amid ongoing strikes by the United States and Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: International Criminal Court briefs on Darfur
UN News.first_paragraph: On Wednesday, the Security Council heard an update on the International Criminal Court's work in Sudan's Darfur region, referred to the Court back in 2005. Focus has recently turned to atrocities in the ongoing war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The briefing was held as the ICC faces mounting pressure: this week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a campaign to “dismantle” the Court, which prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and the crime of aggression. Follow full live coverage below.

UN News.title: New guidance offers hope for reducing the global toll of dementia
UN News.first_paragraph: The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued updated global guidelines aimed at reducing the risk of cognitive decline and dementia, saying that up to 45 per cent of cases may be preventable or delayed by addressing modifiable risk factors throughout life.

UN News.title: Colombia: Pockets of insecurity challenge ‘vibrant democracy’, Security Council told
UN News.first_paragraph: As Colombia awaits the inauguration of its newly elected president, pockets of insecurity remain a challenge for a nation that has overcome decades of conflict, the head of the UN verification team there told the Security Council on Wednesday.

UN News.title: Looted gold and gum arabic are bankrolling Sudan’s war, UN warns
UN News.first_paragraph: Alongside gold, the little-known Sudanese commodity gum arabic – used in soft drinks, food, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals – continues to fuel the war.

UN News.title: Childhood vaccination rate increases slightly, but millions remain unprotected
UN News.first_paragraph: Global childhood immunization programmes continued to recover in 2025, but conflict, poverty and growing vaccine hesitancy are still leaving millions vulnerable to preventable diseases, according to new UN data released on Wednesday.

UN News.title: Skills for an uncertain future: How youth can navigate a changing job market
UN News.first_paragraph: Choosing a path for the future has never been easy, but for young people today, such rapid technological change as artificial intelligence (AI) is making it increasingly difficult to predict which skills will remain relevant in the years ahead.

UN News.title: World Cup football’s other goal: Helping young people talk about mental health
UN News.first_paragraph: When Dr. Sahira Al Nahari founded Shifā Art, a Saudi Arabia-based organization using art to create conversations around mental health, she noticed that men attending her therapeutic art workshops often felt uncomfortable opening up about their feelings.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: Gaza aid challenges persist, renewed push for clean energy, Sudan cholera update
UN News.first_paragraph: Humanitarians in the Gaza Strip continue to face significant challenges in reaching communities located near the so-called “Yellow Line” in northern Rafah, the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Tuesday.

UN News.title: West Africa and the Sahel: Terrorism is changing its face
UN News.first_paragraph: Jihadist groups are no longer content with launching attacks in West Africa and the Sahel: they administer territories, control trade routes, exploit new technologies and are gradually pushing their influence all the way to the Gulf of Guinea.

UN News.title: Independent expert urges UK leaders to uphold Supreme Court ruling on women’s rights
UN News.first_paragraph: A UN independent human rights expert has urged political leaders in the United Kingdom to support implementation of a Supreme Court ruling on the legal definition of sex, warning that opposition to updated equality guidance risks weakening protections for women and girls.

UN News.title: ‘Hunted’ by drones: UN reports worst month for Ukraine’s civilians since 2022
UN News.first_paragraph: Civilian casualties in Ukraine soared during the first half of 2026 amid escalating Russian attacks and intensifying use of deadly weapons, the UN human rights monitoring mission in the country, HRMMU, said on Tuesday.

UN News.title: ‘Cycle of escalation must end’: UN condemns deadly Strait of Hormuz attacks
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN maritime agency, IMO, condemned overnight attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz that killed at least two seafarers as fresh strikes were reported early Tuesday in the escalating US-Iran war.

UN News.title: People continue to stand by refugees, Gen Z shows most empathy
UN News.first_paragraph: Protection for refugees has been enshrined in international law for more than seven decades, but how much support is there today for those fleeing conflict and persecution?

UN News.title: ‘This is a fire’: DRC Ebola outbreak is fastest-growing ever, warns WHO
UN News.first_paragraph: Infections of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have reached record highs and a majority of new cases are coming from “unknown chains of transmission”, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Tuesday.

UN News.title: International Criminal Court ‘a critical cog’ in global justice efforts
UN News.first_paragraph: The United Nations upheld the critical role of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Monday in the global fight to end impunity for grave crimes amid calls for it to be abolished.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: Aid deliveries to Gaza restricted, UN prepares El Nino response, El Salvador eliminates disease
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is calling for greater humanitarian access to Gaza, warning that restrictions on aid deliveries, ongoing violence and funding shortages are severely limiting its ability to reach people in need.

UN News.title: Strait of Hormuz: UN agencies call for diplomacy to end attacks
UN News.first_paragraph: As both Washington and Tehran claim to control the critical commercial shipping route through the narrow Strait of Hormuz, UN agencies on Monday are calling for de-escalation amid the recent spike in strikes in the region related to the US-Iran war.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: Top UN officials call for de-escalation in Yemen
UN News.first_paragraph: As the UN chief’s Special Envoy for Yemen, Hans Grundberg, calls for swift de-escalation following reports of Saudi Arabian airstrikes and Iranian aircraft landing in the country, the Security Council’s emergency meeting at 3pm (local time) on Monday heard briefings from top officials on the latest humanitarian and political situation.

UN News.title: Despite hurdles, don’t give up on Sustainable Development Goals, UN urges
UN News.first_paragraph: In a world of “parallel realities” where stark inequalities seemingly divide people and challenge the promise of multilateralism, the vision of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is to bring people together and help them achieve a better reality.

UN News.title: Afghanistan: 3.7 million young lives at risk of malnutrition, UNICEF warns
UN News.first_paragraph: Some 3.7 million children under five in Afghanistan are at heightened risk of malnutrition due to food insecurity, poor diets and inadequate access to basic services as the peak season for life-threatening wasting looms.

UN News.title: From NASA to the classroom: The engineer bringing AI to those left behind
UN News.first_paragraph: Nia Jetter spent two decades building spacecraft and robots. Now she is trying to make sure the artificial intelligence revolution doesn't leave anyone behind.

UN News.title: UN chief urges Iran and US to ‘urgently resume negotiations’ as Gulf strikes escalate
UN News.first_paragraph: Renewed strikes and counterstrikes between Iran and the United States in the Gulf region have raised fears of a return to all‑out war, with Washington denying Tehran’s claim that it had closed the crucial Strait of Hormuz on Sunday.

UN News.title: Reviving communities home by home in Gaza
UN News.first_paragraph: Displacement has drastically reshaped every aspect of daily life in war-ravaged Gaza for 24-year-old Mayyada, who is seven months pregnant with twins and caring for her two-year-old daughter, but now she and her family are getting settled into a temporary home of their own.

UN News.title: Thai youth leaders push for inclusion, partnership and lasting change
UN News.first_paragraph: From local communities to the global stage, a diverse group of young leaders from Thailand is helping shape conversations on public policy, climate action, inclusion, indigenous rights, disability access and youth wellbeing.

UN News.title: ‘We face a new ordeal’: Gaza's search for the dead goes on
UN News.first_paragraph: After thousands of buildings were destroyed in the Gaza Strip during the Israel-Hamas war, local teams and civil defense personnel continue the arduous and delicate mission to remove rubble and search for the remains of missing persons believed to still be buried under the debris of homes destroyed by Israeli airstrikes.

UN News.title: World News in Brief: UN spotlights education aid solution, Sri Lanka prison violence, humanitarian aid to Venezuela
UN News.first_paragraph: The UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) urged international lenders to expand debt-for-education swaps, warning in a Friday report that many developing countries are spending more on debt servicing than on schooling their children.

UN News.title: South Sudan: UN acts ahead of drought to protect thousands
UN News.first_paragraph: As drought risk intensifies in South Sudan’s Eastern Equatoria state, a new UN-backed plan aims to protect thousands of people before the worst impacts take hold.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: ‘Lost continuity of knowledge’ on Iran’s nuclear programme since US-Israel attacks, top UN official warns
UN News.first_paragraph: Since the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran in late February, there has been a “lost continuity of knowledge” on Tehran’s nuclear programme, Rosemary DiCarlo, the UN peace affairs chief, warned the Security Council on Friday as tensions mounted amid new strikes across the Middle East.

UN News.title: New cholera outbreak alert for Sudan’s war-weary communities
UN News.first_paragraph: In war-torn Sudan, a deadly new cholera outbreak has already claimed more than 100 lives, heightening serious concerns for vulnerable communities including in besieged El-Obeid, where daily drone attacks have continued to hamper aid access.

UN News.title: Aid cuts leave at least one million women and girls without vital support
UN News.first_paragraph: At least one million women and girls have lost access to critical humanitarian support since January 2025 as unprecedented aid cuts push women's organizations in crisis zones to the brink of collapse, the UN’s gender equality agency, UN Women, said on Friday.

UN News.title: Diplomats go virtual to witness Gaza displacement site up close
UN News.first_paragraph: Representatives from 12 countries carried out a “virtual diplomatic field visit” to a displacement site in the Gaza Strip and heard from some of the residents about their pressing needs, the United Nations said on Thursday.

UN News.title: Peak heat in Europe just broke historic 1970s records
UN News.first_paragraph: This year marks the hottest June recorded for Western Europe and the second warmest globally, according to the latest report from a climate tracking service released on Thursday.

UN News.title: World must move faster on Ebola response for DR Congo: UN relief chief
UN News.first_paragraph: The world must move faster to contain the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), UN relief chief Tom Fletcher said on Thursday.

UN News.title: Remembering the Srebrenica genocide: ‘Fear is all that kept me moving’
UN News.first_paragraph: The United Nations paused on Thursday to remember the more than 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys killed in the town of Srebrenica in July 1995, and the women and survivors left to rebuild their lives in the aftermath.

UN News.title: Use of explosive weapons ‘must stop’ in eastern DR Congo: Türk
UN News.first_paragraph: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk urged the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group to cease hostilities as he deplored recent civilian deaths on Thursday.

UN News.title: US-Iran war leaves shipping at near-standstill in Hormuz again
UN News.first_paragraph: Renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran reportedly brought shipping to a near-standstill in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, leaving around 6,000 seafarers stranded aboard hundreds of vessels and Gulf countries on high alert for further attacks.

UN News.title: Security Council LIVE: ‘Urgent de-escalation’ needed now in Ukraine amid spike in civilian deaths
UN News.first_paragraph: The Security Council must use every tool and diplomatic channel to reach an urgent de-escalation, Rosemary DiCarlo, chief of UN political and peacebuilding affairs, told an emergency meeting on Thursday amid escalating deadly Russian drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian civilians.

UN News.title: Srebrenica survivors warn of genocide denial while safeguarding memory of the dead
UN News.first_paragraph: Three survivors of the genocide which took place in Srebrenica in Bosnia and Herzegovina in July 1995 have told UN News how they are keeping alive the memory of the more than 8,300 men and boys who were killed in the town while combating the rising current of denial about the massacre.

UN News.title: Restoring dignity: Senegalese surgeon and Burundian foundation win reproductive health awards
UN News.first_paragraph: A Senegalese surgeon who has dedicated his career to restoring the health and dignity of women living with obstetric fistula, and a Burundian foundation supporting vulnerable women and children, have been named the winners of the 2026 United Nations Population Award.

UN News.title: UN Syria inquiry presses for answers on missing detainees after wide-ranging visit
UN News.first_paragraph: UN investigators have urged Syria’s Government to trace thousands of missing detainees and hold perpetrators to account after a week-long visit that took in bomb attacks in Damascus, prison visits in the northeast and reports of vigilante violence in Homs.
